LESSON: WATER

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Resources in Our Environment
Topic 3.1: Water
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Water, part of Resources in Our Environment in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How can we keep water clean? 2. How can we make water safe for drinking?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. state ways in which water is contaminated in the environment,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Water in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. carry out activities that are used to make water clean,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Water in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. conserve water at home and school as scarce resource,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Water in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. value the importance of clean and safe water for healthy living. ● Learners are guided to brainstorm on sources and uses of water in the environment. ● Learners with low vision observe pictures or watch video clips on how water can be contaminated in the environment (Human activities-washing clothes, bathing, urinating, swimming; Animals- drinking directly from water source, excreting in water sources). Learners with blindness are guided to listen to verbal descriptions of pictures or audio clips on how water can be contaminated in the environment (Human activities-washing clothes, bathing, urinating, swimming; Animals- drinking directly from water source, excreting in water sources). ● Learners with low vision make improvised water filter using locally available materials. Learners with blindness to be given clear verbal descriptions of the procedure followed in making an improvised water filter. 1. How can we keep water clean? 2. How can we make water safe for drinking? 25 ● Learners are guided to use digital devices with assistive technology to search for the procedure of filtering water using different materials such as a piece of cloth, improvised water filter or a sieve. ● In groups, learners clean dirty water through filtration using different materials (a piece of cloth, improvised water filter or a sieve). Learners with blindness to be given a step by step verbal description of how to filter water and carry out the activity with support. ● Learners are guided to discuss how to make water safe for drinking by boiling it. ● In groups, learners are guided to use water in carrying out various activities such as washing clothes, cleaning hands, washing dishes, cleaning vegetables and fruits. ● In groups, learners discuss ways in which water can be reused and share their findings in class (watering plants, washing toilets, sprinkling on earthen surfaces to reduce dust, cleaning outdoor surface

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Water together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
Unity: learner enhances team spirit as they work collaboratively when making a water filter from locally available materials.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: learner enhances unity and cooperation instead of competition as they make improvised filters from locally available

materials.

Link to other learning areas

Making improvised filters from locally available materials can be used by learners when learning about sequencing in mathematics.

Suggested Learning Resources

Approved support learning materials, dirty water, sieves, soil, pebbles, charcoal, pictures.
